bill.title: A resolution designating June 23, 2025, as "Social Media Harms Victim Remembrance Day".
bill.latestActionText: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4511; text: CR S4508)
bill.officialSummary: This resolution designates June 23, 2025, as Social Media Harms Victim Remembrance Day and encourages government, industry, and community stakeholders to take action to prevent social media-related harm.

classification.plainSummary:
This resolution designates June 23, 2025, as Social Media Harms Victim Remembrance Day and encourages government, industry, and community stakeholders to take action to prevent social media-related harm.

This is a measure the Library of Congress labels as a congressional tribute or commemoration. It carries no sector tags and no donor overlap is computed for it, because attributing an economic interest to a commemorative or procedural measure would be misleading.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would name June 23, 2025, as Social Media Harms Victim Remembrance Day and encourage government, industry, and community stakeholders to take action to prevent social media-related harm.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who uses the internet. People who have been the victim of a crime.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what you can do online. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
